items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: they’re standing on the shoulders of these people in my photograph. You know, Dizzy and Mingus and Lester and Coleman Hawkins.

ctx.x: An opera singer could fill it up. Yeah, it’s interesting. What’s your take on jazz today and the future?

Gee I don’t know. I have people I always go and see — Ahmad Jamal, I’m crazy about him. I would like to hear some big bands occasionally. Gosh, Jimmy Heath came by the table yesterday at the Life thing and said that he has a big band playing at the Iridium Room. I thought he said it was just last night. And I was too tired, but I think it’s for the whole week. So and he’s wonderful. But I said something, and I suppose I shouldn’t have said it to a newspaper, and it’s not a very original line, but I said the…
He died awful young, didn’t he?
